# New Benchmarks Show Postgres Dominating MongoDB in Varied Workloads

Performance of two of the fastest-growing database management systems compared head-to-head with Postgres emerging as the winner

BEDFORD, Mass., June 26, 2019 /PRNewswire/ -- The Postgres database management system (DBMS) measured between 4 and 15 times faster than MongoDB in transaction performance testing conducted by [OnGres](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=2508835-1&h=3044466818&u=https%3A%2F%2Fongres.com%2F&a=OnGres), a company specializing in providing database software and services1 and sponsored by EnterpriseDB.

Interestingly, Postgres demonstrated a performance advantage in a JSON (JavaScript Object Notation)-based online analytical processing (OLAP) test designed specifically to focus on document-based data, MongoDB's presumed strength. Additional testing was conducted on online transaction processing (OLTP) workloads. For the OLTP test, the industry standard [sysbench](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=2508835-1&h=3643602004&u=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fakopytov%2Fsysbench&a=sysbench+) benchmark was used to show Postgres performing three times faster than MongoDB on average. Throughout the testing measuring performance on various workloads, Postgres consistently delivered higher performance than MongoDB.

All the code used in testing is open source and available on [GitLab](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=2508835-1&h=287797929&u=https%3A%2F%2Fgitlab.com%2Fongresinc%2Fbenchplatform&a=GitLab) so others can independently reproduce and audit the results. In addition, the testing methodology and results are [available for download today](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=2508835-1&h=1368101754&u=https%3A%2F%2Finfo.enterprisedb.com%2FPerformance-Benchmarks-PostgreSQL-vs-MongoDB.html&a=available+for+download+today).

"The benchmark was designed to be reproducible and run on a public cloud, so anyone who wants to compare Postgres and MongoDB can easily do so," said Alvaro Hernandez, founder of OnGres. "We're sharing all the information on the tests we ran, why they were selected and the results we found so that anyone can reproduce the results or change parameters and configurations for their own needs."

The GitLab project includes two repositories which allow a comparison of the performance of Postgres 11.1 and MongoDB 4.0 running on Amazon Web Services (AWS). The goal of the benchmark was to compare the performance of Postgres and MongoDB in several different use cases while simulating real-life production scenarios as much as possible. The tests analyze the capabilities and performance of Postgres and MongoDB using the same data design across a range of active dataset sizes. Both public and generated datasets were used.
